summary: Stream claim backups to stdout with a complete-output checksum receipt and a bounded WAL growth guard

replay.detail: No replay or backfill. Offline stdout export requires cleanly stopped, checkpointed input and refuses nonempty graph or messages-shard WALs, migration, sealing, repair or projection recovery.

schema.detail: No database schema or claim registry change.

rules.detail: No claim admission, authority or projection rule change.

compatibility.detail: fractal backup create - streams the existing archive JSONL to stdout. Live export uses /v1/backup?stream=true&max_wal_growth=4294967296 and a bounded channel without an archive tempfile. Only complete verified records reach stdout. Optional source writer identity/store-index metadata and end-record aggregate/per-file peak WAL growth do not require an archive version bump. Existing file-destination mode and file-based restore are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No deployment downtime or startup migration. Offline stdout export requires a cleanly stopped and checkpointed graph and messages shard; keep the daemon stopped throughout the immutable read.

manual.detail: Save stdout to a private file before restore. Successful stdout export emits a JSON receipt on stderr with format, version, records, sha256, bytes, writer_id, max_store_index, started_at, finished_at, peak_wal_growth and peak_wal_growth_by_file. The receipt checksum covers all stdout, including the end record; the archive end checksum still covers preceding bytes only. Check every pipeline exit status and discard partial output after failure. --max-wal-growth limits the sampled sum of growth across every pinned graph/shard WAL, default 4294967296 bytes (4 GiB); exceeding it aborts without a successful receipt. Per-file peaks identify graph and shards/messages. Offline --database stdout mode uses mode=ro&immutable=1, refuses nonempty WALs, requires compatible fully sealed healthy state and persisted writer identity, and leaves database, WAL, SHM and directory entries unchanged.

recovery.detail: Restore still reads a file and verifies archive checksums and restored graph/log digests. The source writer identity is not a physical database UUID.
